stories.headline: U.S.-China trade truce extended for two months, Bessent says, as Xi begins state visit
stories.dek: The truce extension landed on the first day of Xi Jinping's state visit.
tldr: Bessent said the US-China trade truce has been extended for two months as Xi Jinping began a state visit, CNBC reported.
Investing.com carried the same development as Trump welcomed Xi.
A widely shared r/wallstreetbets post cited Bessent as saying the truce was extended to Jan. 10.

body.text: The US-China trade truce was extended for two months, Bessent said, as Xi began his state visit, CNBC reported.
Investing.com reported that the US says the China trade truce was extended as Trump welcomes Xi.
A post on r/wallstreetbets cited Bessent as saying the two sides agreed to extend the truce to Jan. 10.

stories.whyItMatters: A two-month extension defers rather than resolves tariff risk for supply chains and earnings guidance, and the new deadline becomes the next event date for markets. It also sets the tone for the state visit covered in Geopolitics.
stories.editorNote: The Jan. 10 date comes from a Reddit post attributing it to Bessent and was not confirmed in the other headlines; the terms of the extension were not in the collected data. No investment view is expressed.

stories.headline: Mark Zuckerberg debuts $1,299 Meta VR Glasses and Muse Charm pendant amid AI agent push
stories.dek: Meta put new hardware behind its Muse assistant.
tldr: Zuckerberg unveiled $1,299 Meta VR Glasses and a Muse Charm pendant amid Meta's AI agent push, CNBC reported.
Investing.com reported Meta debuted a new handheld device dedicated to using Muse.
The headlines do not make clear whether the handheld device and the Muse Charm pendant are the same product.

body.text: Mark Zuckerberg debuted $1,299 Meta VR Glasses and a Muse Charm pendant amid Meta's AI agent push, CNBC reported.
Investing.com reported that Meta debuted a new handheld device dedicated to using Muse.

stories.whyItMatters: Dedicated hardware for Meta's Muse assistant extends the AI-agent race from software into devices, putting Meta more directly against phone platforms for the default AI interface and raising the spending stakes behind its AI push.
stories.editorNote: Shipping dates and pricing beyond the $1,299 glasses were not in the collected data. No investment view is expressed.

stories.headline: 30-year Treasury yield hits highest level since 2004
stories.dek: Long-dated U.S. borrowing costs rose to levels last seen in 2004 as the global bond selloff continued.
tldr: CNBC reported that the 30-year Treasury yield reached its highest level since 2004.
Reuters reported a rise above 5.44% as bond prices fell.
The reports linked the move to stronger growth and inflation concerns and shifting expectations for Federal Reserve rates.

body.text: CNBC reported that the 30-year Treasury yield reached its highest level since 2004.
Reuters reported the yield rose more than three basis points to 5.444% as prices fell.
Reuters attributed the move in part to stronger U.S. growth and inflation signals, which increased expectations of Federal Reserve rate hikes.

stories.whyItMatters: Higher long-term government borrowing costs affect financing conditions across the economy; this report describes the market move and does not give an investment view.
stories.editorNote: Reuters coverage is carried by MarketScreener. Yield figures vary by time of observation; 5.444% is Reuters’ reported intraday level.

stories.headline: New York Fed’s Williams says it's 'reasonable' to expect another rate hike by year-end
stories.dek: New York Fed President John Williams said another rate increase by year-end was a reasonable expectation, while a former Dallas Fed chief argued markets may be pricing too many hikes.
tldr: CNBC reported Williams said another rate hike by year-end was “reasonable” to expect.
MarketWatch reported former Dallas Fed chief Robert Kaplan’s view that markets were pricing in too many Fed hikes.
The two reports show a disagreement over the rate outlook, not a Federal Reserve decision.

body.text: Williams said it was reasonable to expect another rate hike by year-end, CNBC reported.
MarketWatch reported that former Dallas Fed chief Robert Kaplan believes markets are pricing in too many Fed hikes.
These are individual views; neither report announces a change to the Federal Open Market Committee’s target range.

stories.whyItMatters: Different readings of the policy outlook can move yields and expectations even before the Federal Reserve makes a decision.
stories.editorNote: No rate forecast is made here; the story attributes each view to its speaker and outlet.

stories.headline: Oil prices rise sharply as investors seek progress on U.S.-Iran talks
stories.dek: Oil prices rose as traders watched for progress in U.S.-Iran talks; separate coverage also described continuing gains.
tldr: CNBC reported oil prices rose sharply as investors sought progress in U.S.-Iran talks.
Investing.com separately reported that oil extended gains amid limited signs of progress.
The reports connect the price move to geopolitical developments but do not establish a lasting supply change.

body.text: CNBC reported rising oil prices as investors looked for progress in U.S.-Iran talks.
Investing.com also reported oil extending gains, describing little sign of progress in the talks.
The headlines do not quantify a durable change in supply or provide a price forecast.

stories.whyItMatters: Energy prices can respond to perceived geopolitical supply risk, making the status of negotiations relevant to market volatility.
stories.editorNote: No oil price target or trading recommendation is offered.
